session.title: Authorization defect classification for account deletion

messages.text:
PHASE11_CASE_E_FRESH_ROOT

This is an isolated fresh-root qualification run for a bounded security defect classification.

The disposable worktree and starting HEAD were externally verified immediately before this OpenCode root was started:

repository root:
C:\Users\BLAUTECH\AppData\Local\Temp\olympus-phase11-case-e

starting HEAD:
314a6bc529e0d5e17d1662e3765734b7cc80cd86

Do not spawn a qualification worker solely to repeat that isolation check unless actual runtime evidence contradicts these supplied facts.

Classify this bounded hypothetical defect:

A user with role MEMBER can delete another user's account, while the stated authorization contract allows account deletion only to ADMIN.

The observed behavior is treated as established for this qualification. You do not need to reproduce or exploit it.

Use the smallest sufficient security-specific route.

Explain:

- the violated authorization/trust boundary;
- why this is materially security-specific rather than an ordinary functional bug;
- the safe expected authorization invariant;
- a bounded, non-exploitative validation strategy for a future fix;
- any important regression cases required to establish that MEMBER remains denied and ADMIN remains allowed.

Do NOT:

- attempt an exploit;
- execute destructive actions;
- modify files;
- implement a fix;
- broaden into a repository-wide security audit;
- inspect unrelated source;
- use FAST;
- optimize;
- enter `/maintain`;
- commit, stage, push, merge, tag, or release.

This is a diagnosis/classification task only.

Do not route to Argus merely because the request contains the word "bug".

Do not invoke Kovan because no implementation is authorized.

Do not invoke Thales unless a genuinely high-uncertainty diagnostic condition unexpectedly emerges from new evidence; the supplied authorization boundary is intentionally explicit.

content.text:
WORKTREE_ISOLATION:
SUPPLIED_VERIFIED

SECURITY_CLASSIFICATION:
CONFIRMED_SECURITY_DEFECT under the supplied established behavior: authorization bypass. Unauthorized deletion violates account integrity and availability, making this materially security-specific rather than merely incorrect functional behavior.

VIOLATED_BOUNDARY:
A MEMBER crosses the server-enforced privilege boundary protecting ADMIN-only account deletion and acts on another user’s account.

EXPECTED_INVARIANT:
Account deletion requires an authenticated, authorized ADMIN. MEMBER requests must be denied without deletion side effects, regardless of target account or caller-supplied role claims.

SAFE_VALIDATION:
For a future fix, use synthetic identities and mocked deletion operations; no real accounts or exploit attempts. Verify:
- MEMBER deleting another account: denied; deletion operation never invoked.
- MEMBER deleting their own account: denied under the stated ADMIN-only contract.
- Changing target identifiers or supplying an ADMIN role claim cannot bypass denial.
- Anonymous, missing-role, and other non-ADMIN callers: denied.
- Authenticated ADMIN deleting a valid permitted target: allowed; mocked deletion invoked as expected.
- Every supported deletion entry point enforces the same invariant.
